You design and build LEGO Technic models one step at a time, in a build language.

Before every step you think in THINK lines: what is already built and what it does, the goal of this step, each new part and where it goes, what it touches, the mechanism rule it must follow, why these parts, each part's role in the finished machine, every join (which hole, how deep, locked / turns / stiff), what it builds on from earlier steps, how complete each mechanism is, and what it sets up later.

Then you write the moves:
ADD name partnumber color
CONNECT part.point -> part.point LOCKED|TURNS|STIFF   (points: hole1.., axlehole1.., pin1.., axle1.., clip1..; LOCKED = cross in cross, turn together; TURNS = free; STIFF = friction pin)
MESH a.teeth b.teeth / RATIO a b x/y / DOES a VERB b (HOLDS, CARRIES, SPINS_ON, DRIVES, LOCKS, SUPPORTS) / GROUP g ... END / ATTACH g / PATTERN name
Then the mechanism lines: MECH id type part role / STATE id n/m [COMPLETE] / MOTION input part=turns ...
A point ending in ~ is an estimate; ? means not known.

Rules: only use real points of each part; a round pin never goes in a cross hole; a shaft that must turn needs round holes; a worm needs stops on both sides; gears must sit at the right distance; every part must have a job in a mechanism or the structure.

SET LEGO Technic 8047 Compact Excavator
PARTS SO FAR none
LAST STEPS

Write main step 1. Think first (THINK lines), then the moves, then the mechanism lines.

THINK have Nothing yet.
THINK goal Starts a straight cross shaft for the middle of the undercarriage.
THINK part rod-A (32054 Technic Pin Long with Stop Bush): first part; long pin lying left to right, ring (stop bush) end on the right; fixed
THINK part axle-A (4519 Technic Axle 3): pushed into the axle hole in rod-A's ring end; fixed
THINK touches axle-A goes into the axle hole in rod-A's ring end
THINK does rod-A holds axle-A
THINK need rigid_frame: Structure that keeps everything at the right distance. Not a moving mechanism, but every mechanism depends on it. Rules: A joint with one pin can swing: use two pins, an axle in cross holes, or close a triangle/rectangle. Shafts' bearings must sit in the frame at the gear spacing.
THINK why A long pin with a stop ring has a pin on one end (to hang beams on) and an axle hole on the other (to join an axle).
THINK role rod-A in the undercarriage frame: Near end of the back cross shaft; its pin end carries bentbeam-I (step 5) and the near side rail beam9-Y (step 12).
THINK role axle-A in the undercarriage frame: The spine of the cross shaft: carries beam-C in the middle and joins rod-A to rod-B.
THINK check axle-A.axle1 goes into rod-A.axlehole1, 1 hole deep, locked (turn together)
THINK mechanism axle-A becomes the spine of the cross shaft of the undercarriage frame
THINK state frame has 1 of 8 parts, still missing beam-C, bentbeam-D, bentbeam-I, beam7-N, beam-R, beam9-X, beam9-Y
THINK later rod-A's pin end will hold a bent beam (step 5) and a side rail (step 12). Pattern: pin-axle-pin shaft
STEP 1
ADD rod-A 32054 black
ADD axle-A 4519 lightgray
CONNECT axle-A.axle1 -> rod-A.axlehole1 LOCKED
DOES rod-A HOLDS axle-A
PATTERN pin_axle_pin_shaft
MECH frame rigid_frame axle-A spine_of_the
STATE frame 1/8

Write main step 2. Think first (THINK lines), then the moves, then the mechanism lines.

THINK have rod-A with axle-A sticking out of its ring end.
THINK goal Finishes the cross shaft and gives it a mounting point in the middle.
THINK part beam-C (63869 Technic Axle and Pin Connector Perpendicular Triple): on axle-A next to rod-A's ring, three pin holes facing down; fixed
THINK part rod-B (32054 Technic Pin Long with Stop Bush): on the free end of axle-A, ring end inward, pin end pointing out; fixed
THINK touches beam-C slides onto axle-A through its top axle hole
THINK touches rod-B's ring end pushes onto axle-A's free end
THINK does axle-A carries beam-C
THINK does rod-B holds axle-A
THINK does rod-A and rod-B lock beam-C in place between their rings
THINK need rigid_frame: Structure that keeps everything at the right distance. Not a moving mechanism, but every mechanism depends on it. Rules: A joint with one pin can swing: use two pins, an axle in cross holes, or close a triangle/rectangle. Shafts' bearings must sit in the frame at the gear spacing.
THINK why The triple connector turns one axle into three pin holes facing sideways; the two rings trap it so it can't slide.
THINK role beam-C in the undercarriage frame: Turns the cross shaft into pin holes facing back, so the turntable can be pinned to the frame (via pin-E, pin-F in step 8).
THINK role rod-B in the undercarriage frame: Far end of the cross shaft; carries bentbeam-D (step 3) and the far side rail beam9-X (step 12).
THINK check axle-A.axle2 goes into beam-C.axlehole1, 1 hole deep, locked (turn together)
THINK check axle-A.axle3 goes into rod-B.axlehole1, 1 hole deep, locked (turn together)
THINK builds_on beam-C builds on axle-A (8047-step-01), which is the spine of the cross shaft in the undercarriage frame, and rests on rod-A (8047-step-01)
THINK builds_on rod-B builds on axle-A (8047-step-01), which is the spine of the cross shaft in the undercarriage frame, and rests on rod-A (8047-step-01)
THINK mechanism beam-C becomes the mount for the turntable pins of the undercarriage frame
THINK state frame has 2 of 8 parts, still missing bentbeam-D, bentbeam-I, beam7-N, beam-R, beam9-X, beam9-Y
THINK later beam-C's holes take the two pins that hold the turntable (steps 3 and 8). Pattern: trapped connector on a shaft

ADD beam-C 63869 lightgray
CONNECT axle-A.axle2 -> beam-C.axlehole1 LOCKED
ADD rod-B 32054 black
CONNECT axle-A.axle3 -> rod-B.axlehole1 LOCKED
DOES axle-A CARRIES beam-C
DOES rod-B HOLDS axle-A
DOES rod-A LOCKS beam-C
DOES rod-B LOCKS beam-C
PATTERN trapped_connector
MECH frame rigid_frame beam-C mount_for_the
STATE frame 2/8

Write main step 3. Think first (THINK lines), then the moves, then the mechanism lines.

THINK have Straight shaft (rod-A, axle-A, rod-B) with beam-C in the middle.
THINK goal Starts one side of the front frame and readies the turntable mount.
THINK part bentbeam-D (32140 Technic Beam 2 x 4 L-Shape Thick): on rod-B's pin end, long arm pointing forward, short arm up at the shaft; fixed
THINK part pin-E (2780 Technic Pin with Friction Ridges): in one outer hole of beam-C, pointing backward; fixed
THINK part pin-F (2780 Technic Pin with Friction Ridges): in the other outer hole of beam-C, pointing backward; fixed
THINK touches bentbeam-D's short-arm end hole slides over rod-B's pin end (red arrow)
THINK touches pin-E and pin-F go into beam-C's two outer pin holes
THINK does rod-B holds bentbeam-D
THINK does beam-C holds pin-E and pin-F
THINK need rigid_frame: Structure that keeps everything at the right distance. Not a moving mechanism, but every mechanism depends on it. Rules: A joint with one pin can swing: use two pins, an axle in cross holes, or close a triangle/rectangle. Shafts' bearings must sit in the frame at the gear spacing.
THINK why An L-shaped beam goes up and over the shaft, then runs forward; two pins give a firm two-point grip.
THINK role bentbeam-D in the undercarriage frame: Right side of the front U; reaches forward to the front cross beam.
THINK role pin-E in the undercarriage frame: One of the two pins the turntable's fixed half sits on (step 8).
THINK role pin-F in the undercarriage frame: The other turntable pin.
THINK check rod-B.pin2 goes into bentbeam-D.hole4, 0.9 hole deep, held stiff by friction
THINK check pin-E.pin1 goes into beam-C.hole1, 0.9 hole deep, held stiff by friction
THINK check pin-F.pin1 goes into beam-C.hole3, 0.9 hole deep, held stiff by friction
THINK builds_on bentbeam-D builds on rod-B (8047-step-02), and rests on axle-A (8047-step-01)
THINK builds_on pin-E builds on beam-C (8047-step-02), which is the mount for the turntable pins in the undercarriage frame, and rests on axle-A (8047-step-01)
THINK builds_on pin-F builds on beam-C (8047-step-02), which is the mount for the turntable pins in the undercarriage frame, and rests on axle-A (8047-step-01)
THINK mechanism bentbeam-D becomes the far side member of the undercarriage frame
THINK state frame has 3 of 8 parts, still missing bentbeam-I, beam7-N, beam-R, beam9-X, beam9-Y
THINK later pin-E and pin-F hold the turntable in step 8; bentbeam-D's front end takes a connector in step 4. Pattern: two-pin mount (stops twisting)
STEP 3
ADD bentbeam-D 32140 black
CONNECT rod-B.pin2 -> bentbeam-D.hole4 STIFF
ADD pin-E 2780 black
CONNECT pin-E.pin1 -> beam-C.hole1 STIFF
ADD pin-F 2780 black
CONNECT pin-F.pin1 -> beam-C.hole3 STIFF
DOES rod-B HOLDS bentbeam-D
DOES beam-C HOLDS pin-E
DOES beam-C HOLDS pin-F
PATTERN two_pin_mount
MECH frame rigid_frame bentbeam-D far_side_member
STATE frame 3/8

MESH a.teeth b.teeth / RATIO a b x/y / DOES a VERB b (HOLDS, CARRIES, SPINS_ON, DRIVES, LOCKS, SUPPORTS) / GROUP g ... END / ATTACH g / PATTERN name
